referencesLine.message: Drop "References available upon request" — it wastes space; employers request references separately.

objectiveSection.message: A career-objective line is optional and most useful for 1st/2nd-year students with limited internships; final-year students with real experience should drop it.

excludeIndia.message: Drop personal fields not relevant to professional evaluation (DOB, gender, religion, full home address).

dateConsistency.message: Use one date format throughout (don't mix "Sept." with "September", or exact months with year-only).

atsChecks.message: Two-column / sidebar layouts scramble reading order for ATS parsers — the one confirmed high-impact ATS breaker in controlled testing. Use a single column.
Put contact info in the body of page one, not only in a repeated page header/footer — some ATS engines discard header/footer content.
Use conventional section names (Experience, Education, Skills) — creative headings are missed by ATS section detection.

atsNonIssues.note: Controlled testing showed these parse cleanly — do not flag them despite common folklore.

weakPhrases.message: Replace vague duty phrasing with a specific action verb and a specific, concrete task.

genericTaskFlags.message: State the specific work done, not a generic label — recruiters explicitly call out unspecific "legal research" bullets.

redFlags.message: An unexplained date gap between entries reads as a red flag — address it briefly if real.
Boilerplate, non-specific phrasing reads as AI-generated to recruiters and costs interviews — every bullet should carry a specific, concrete detail unique to the candidate.

positiveSignals.note: A focused, declared practice-area interest with matching internships outperforms an unfocused spread — mirrors the Practice Compass fit logic.

knownGaps: Firm-specific / practice-area-specific screening criteria beyond general Tier-1 corporate-firm signals
Litigation-chamber-side hiring criteria specifically (this pass surfaced firm-side data more than chamber-side)
